title: AC1021 HATCH output proof after entity writers restore caller handles

source.provenanceLimit: Existing local user corpus; producer and repository provenance are unauthenticated. The source was not added or modified.

finding.regression: The DWG-to-DXF adapter's HATCH graph callback required the borrowed entity object's handle to remain equal to its planned emitted handle after the writer returned. Entity writer transaction scopes now restore caller-owned handles, so valid HATCH boundary entities were emitted and recorded but the stale object-state assertion marked the graph invalid and refused the completed DXF.
finding.correction: Validate the planned emitted handle against dxfRW::remapEntityHandle(sourceHandle), and require exactly one published source-entity handle in the writer ledger. Finalization separately checks the emitted record identity, owner and section.
finding.behavior: Strict conversion of the hash-bound AC1021 tablet source now completes and its resulting DXF imports and re-exports at the same version.

implementation.scope: HATCH boundary graph publication proof only; source-handle restoration and strict graph checks remain intact.

physicalConversion.result: PASS; strict conversion published the DXF

freshReadback.result: PASS; fresh DXF import and same-version re-export succeeded

validation.fixturePolicy: No DWG or DXF fixture was added. Conversion outputs remain under /tmp; the generated HATCH/CIRCLE control creates its source in test scratch.

limitations: The physical source is unauthenticated local corpus data and establishes only this source profile.
Fresh libdxfrw readback is transport evidence, not native FreeCAD or LibreCAD acceptance.
No DWG/DXF support claim is promoted; broader P4/P8 graph, semantic and platform gates remain open.
